comparator.name: French Language and Culture
comparator.academicYear: Indicative prospectus pathway: 2027–2028 year 1, 2028–2029 year 2 and 2029–2030 year 3
comparator.sourceNotes: The settled illustrative 180-EC French pathway is preserved: twelve required 5-EC first-year courses; six required 5-EC second-year courses and two restricted 15-EC Faculty of Arts minors; and third-year required francophone-university study 15 EC, professional-world course 5 EC, free choices 30 EC and thesis 10 EC. Zero-credit mentoring and language testing remain excluded. Additional programme-specific minor options remain optional and are not instantiated as mandatory major content. Checked 13 October 2026 against the official overview and three year pages. Their current labels are 2027–2028, 2028–2029 and 2029–2030 respectively; this corrects stale year-three source metadata, not any component, status or credit weight. The French direction within Romance Languages and Cultures is explicit. The public pages are provisional prospectus information, not a finalized external schedule for the Fall 2026 UCR cohort.
components: In the Footsteps of the French Language
Restricted selection of a 15-EC Faculty of Arts minor, one in each semester. The programme lists supplementary French-related minors as optional examples, not compulsory content.
Second restricted 15-EC Faculty of Arts minor; content left open rather than inventing elective courses.
Required study at a francophone university
Compulsory major credit during study abroad, distinct from the accompanying free elective space.
Genuine open elective space, partly available during the period abroad; a placement is among permitted possibilities.
Bachelor Thesis in French Language or Culture
Required individual project may focus on linguistics, literature or cultural studies.

routeSelection.basis: The exact normalized target is French Language and Culture. The current official overview identifies it as the French direction within Romance Languages and Cultures, with French and Spanish selected before entry. Preserve the French pathway; do not substitute Spanish or a generic Romance curriculum. Checked 13 October 2026.

core: Literature, text analysis and creative cultural expression
Art, film, cultural history and varied French-speaking cultural worlds
Culture, politics and society; France within Europe and international institutions
questions: How cultural forms express identity and transmit historical memory

trace: directly teaches practical criticism and interpretation of fiction, poetry and drama; these are literary methods, not French-language proficiency
provides specific complementary argumentation and persuasive writing/presentation skills for critical cultural interpretation; it is not spoken or written French training
provides specific complementary theories of race, class, gender and institutions for analysing cultural identity and social relations
directly studies literary texts, genres and recurring cultural themes across Western heritage; it supplies comparative literary formation rather than a dedicated francophone canon
directly analyses linguistic choices and textual meaning through stylistics, supporting text analysis but not French grammar or translation
provides specific complementary qualitative inquiry into social meaning, research questions and interpretive power relations, supporting the study of culturally situated identities

provides specific complementary theories of international institutions and North–South relations for the evidenced France/international-organisations direction; it does not teach French diplomatic history or language
provides specific complementary historical study of European sovereignty, industrialisation, wars, decolonisation and European cooperation for interpreting modern cultural and political change
directly supplies film-form, narration and visual representation analysis for the target-supported film and popular-cultural direction
directly develops visual analysis of Western paintings, styles and cultural institutions; this is broader European/American art study, not a focused French art-history sequence
provides specific complementary analysis of books and pre-digital objects as technologies of cultural production, circulation and memory
directly examines autobiography, memoir and travel narrative as constructions of identity and cultural memory, supporting literary/cultural self-representation

provides specific complementary analysis of African artistic traditions, colonial acquisition and repatriation, addressing cultural difference and heritage exchange relevant to a programme whose evidenced cultural worlds include Africa; African art is not equated with francophone art
directly studies the documentary representation of people and historical/social contexts, its ethical/aesthetic choices and practical documentary construction
provides specific complementary philosophical analysis of emotion toward fiction and art and aesthetic/moral response; this is one interpretive contribution rather than the central programme theme
directly analyses literary-to-film adaptation, narrative form and intertextuality, contributing the evidenced literature/film connection without claiming French film specialization
directly studies modern art, museum presentation and curatorial practices as institutions shaping cultural interpretation
provides specific complementary historical/theoretical analysis of empires and power for studying cultural influence and exchange; it is not a France-only colonial history

directly studies EU actors, institutions, decision-making and a legislative-dossier research exercise, contributing to the evidenced European institutional setting without claiming a France-specific politics sequence
directly applies interpretive literary theories through a research project, including minority, feminist, Marxist and psychoanalytic readings
directly studies and practices poetic form and creative meaning-making through reading, reflection and performance; this is not creative writing in French

directly researches the 1809 Walcheren expedition involving French, Dutch and British forces through primary diaries, letters and reports, providing an actual France-linked historical case and source-based methods
directly studies art-historical methods, authorship and identity, including documented French theorists Foucault and Derrida; it does not promise a full French intellectual-history course

alternatives.label: Literature, art & cultural history
alternatives.concept: Study literary and visual expression through text analysis, film, art and museums, alongside cultural history and qualitative social inquiry. Two politics courses examine European and international institutions. This related-fields programme develops cultural interpretation; it provides neither French proficiency and translation nor a sustained francophone regional curriculum.
alternatives.labelReason: Five literature, three communication, three media and four art/heritage courses provide the cultural centre. Three history courses, two sociology courses, one philosophy course and two politics courses supply specified historical, interpretive and institutional contributions. The title does not claim French or francophone-specialist formation.
progression: All formal prerequisites and exact workbook terms pass. Literary and rhetorical foundations precede stylistics/creative work and advanced interpretation; film introduction precedes documentary and adaptation; art introduction precedes museums and art historiography; sociology precedes qualitative inquiry; modern history precedes empire and the research seminar. African Art is assigned to its sole cohort offering in 2028h1, and the final literary/art-historiography courses to their actual 2029h1 offerings. No advisory progression signal is promoted into an invented prerequisite.

candidates.label: French linguistics and advanced language acquisition

selection.assessment: One complete related-fields cultural response is defensible. Literary/art/cultural-history interests are substantively represented by the completed core; another label does not establish a different curriculum. The first additional language-science concept fails: Psycholinguistics after its brain/behaviour gateway and stylistics provide only limited language-processing/text-analysis contributions, with no French proficiency, structure, acquisition sequence or sustained multilingualism study. Legal/administrative translation was assessed separately: EU/public/private law and Dutch can supply discrete domain knowledge, but the workbook contains no French language or translation methods; expanding law does not implement this direction. The France/Europe/international-organisations interest has two specific core courses; no evidence establishes an additional complete international-politics route with the required distinct target-grounded course consequences. Stop at one, without attempting a third. Professional qualification is not used as the academic failure criterion.

blocks: Both directly develop literary/textual analysis; the UCR course is comparative and English-medium rather than French textual work.

notes.text: Radboud combines French proficiency, linguistics and francophone literature/culture with translation, required francophone-university study and a thesis. This UCR programme studies related literary, visual and historical questions through literature, film, art, history and social inquiry, with European/international institutional contributions. It does not provide French proficiency, French–Dutch translation, required francophone immersion or a sustained francophone regional curriculum.
